parsed.why: No trans-specific offence: impersonation law repealed; entrenched third-gender tradition, society described as tolerant of trans people, no documented targeting or visitor-facing restriction. Unenforced sodomy statute is a latent tangential factor only, keeping it a step below full-protection states.

No criminalisation, no police targeting, open Pride culture, conversion-therapy ban, broad equality protections, no documented border friction. Restroom discrimination and the resident-only surgery rule are real but mostly resident-facing; rising anti-gender politics is climate, not traveller exposure.

No criminalisation, yet routine refusal of medical care (including general treatment), pervasive hostility outside cities, commonplace lynchings with police non-pursuit, no anti-discrimination law, no recognition, no recourse. Documented tier-3 hostility with thin institutions; violence frequency unresolved but service denial is traveller-facing.

Decriminalised since 1998, hate-speech and hate-crime provisions naming gender identity, conversion-practices ban, civil unions, one region operating self-determination recognition. Offsets: no general gender-identity discrimination ground, inconsistent enforcement with attacks drawing no police action, no documented social acceptance data.

No criminalisation and retained gender-reassignment discrimination protection, but state-imposed universal exposures: birth-sex strip-search policy, in-force single-sex spaces code excluding trans people, birth-sex custody placement, ward exclusion with a documented fatal case; UN warnings unremedied, legal challenge unresolved.
